items.title: Microsoft Research発「TokenEconomizer」がコーディングエージェントのトークン代を18.4〜30.9%削減。モデルを変えずにリポジトリ経験から無駄を学習する仕組みを一次情報から整理する
items.summary:
Microsoft Research発「TokenEconomizer」がコーディングエージェントのトークン代を18.4〜30.9%削減。モデルを変えずにリポジトリ経験から無駄を学習する仕組みを一次情報から整理する

コーディングエージェントの利用が広がるにつれ、「同じリポジトリで繰り返し作業するときのトークン浪費」が実務的な課題になってきた。モデルの単価は下がりつつある一方で、エージェントは毎回ツール定義や過去の調査結果を再請求するため、連続タスクではコストが積み上がる。

これに対してMicrosoft Research、UC Berkeley、Microsoft Securityの研究チームが2026年10月に公開したのがTokenEconomizerだ。Apache-2.0ライセンスのプラグインで、エージェントのモデルやコードを一切変更せず、同じリポジトリの過去セッションから経験を蓄積し、次のセッションの無駄を削る。対応エージェントはClaude Code、Codex、GitHub Copilot CLI、Piで、opencodeやCursor Agent、Grok Build、Hermes Agent、Antigravity CLIも実験的にサポートされている。

【日本語圏での露出】
Zenn、Qiita、はてなブックマークを中心に確認したところ、TokenEconomizerに特化した詳細記事はまだ少ない。noteに個人による紹介が10月末に数件見られた程度で、技術コミュニティでの本格的な検証や比較はこれから、という状況だ。Yahoo!リアルタイム検索でも目立った議論は確認できなかった。

【背景と問題設定】
論文「TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents」（arXiv 2610.22732、2026年10月15日公開）は、従来のトークン効率評価が単発タスクに偏っている点を指摘する。実際の開発では同じコードベースに対して連続してタスクを振るため、環境依存の繰り返しコストが発生する。

著者らは未修正エージェントの60タスクをプロファイリングし、3種類の浪費を特定した。
1. 同じ事実の再発見：5タスク以上進んだリポジトリではツール呼び出しの30%が過去タスクの行動を繰り返す。
2. 未使用ツールの支払い：23のツール定義のうち16が一度も呼ばれないのに毎回送信される。
3. 失敗ループ：失敗する17%のタスクが全支出の32%を占める。

固定戦略（RTKの出力圧縮、Serenaのコードナビ、RepoMapのリポジトリマップ）はリポジトリによって効果が出たり出なかったりし、どのリポジトリでも安くなる単一手法は存在しなかった。

【仕組み：3つのブラックボックス制御】
TokenEconomizerはエージェントをブラックボックスとして扱い、エージェントがすでに公開している表面（セッション開始時のコンテキスト、ツール設定、イベントストリーム）だけを操作する。学習内容はローカルの~/.tokeneconomizerに保存され、独自のAPIキーは不要。プラグイン自身のモデル呼び出しもユーザーの既存ログイン経由で行われ、コストに含まれる。

1. Micro-skills（マイクロスキル注入）
リポジトリ固有の事実（先に実行すべきビルドステップ、python -m pytestのように動くコマンドの書き方、必要な環境変数など）を学習する。失敗の繰り返しと、k=3セッションごとにモデルが過去トレースをレビューして提案する事実を組み合わせる。3セッションで確認された事実はセッション開始時に注入し、後のセッションで矛盾すれば削除する。

2. Tool pruning（ツール剪定）
p=10プロンプト以上、またはm=2セッション以上で未使用のツール、またはs=5セッションで未使用のツールを、エージェントの設定経由で次セッションから除外する。shell、read、editなどのコアツールは常に残す。1コマンドで復帰可能。

3. Failure-loop intervention（ループガード）
ターン内で同じ失敗が続く場合、ルールベースで検出し、信頼度c=0.7以上のLLMジャッジが「stuck」と判断したら1回だけリダイレクトノートを挿入。それでも繰り返せば停止方法をユーザーに通知する（自らは止めない）。成功したターン数の90パーセンタイル×1.25をターン予算の目安にする。

【実験結果】
SWE-Benchの277タスク（6リポジトリ）を5つのagent-model組み合わせで、リポジトリ内のタスクを順に実行して測定した。コストにはTokenEconomizer自身のモデル呼び出しを含む。

- 平均コスト削減：18.4%〜30.9%
- 全30セル（6リポジトリ × 5組み合わせ）ですべてDefaultより安い（リポジトリ内では5〜40%減）
- Pass@1は5組み合わせ中4で向上（Opus 4.8のみ1ポイント低下）
- 具体例：Claude Code + Opus 4.8で-30.9%、Claude Code + Sonnet 5で-23.6%、Codex + GPT-5.6 Terraで-24.7%、Copilot CLI + Sonnet 5で-18.4%

Web-Benchでは16〜21%減、セキュリティ監査ベンチ（新リポジトリが多い）では6〜20%減と、タスク構造によって効果は変動する。プロジェクトページではインタラクティブなチャートと9つの注釈付き実行例が公開されている。

【実務的な影響とバランス】
同じリポジトリで日常的にエージェントを使う開発者にとって、追加のAPI費用なしで導入できる点は実用的だ。データはローカル完結で、失敗時は何もせず通常動作に戻る設計になっている。

一方で限界もある。
- 効果は学習が進むにつれて出るため、単発や新規リポジトリでは薄い。
- テストされたエージェントバージョン範囲（Claude Code 2.1.300〜2.1.310など）を超えると未検証。
- ループガードは停止を強制しないため、ユーザー側の監視は残る。
- Pass@1がわずかに下がるケースもあり、コストと成功率のトレードオフは個別に確認する必要がある。

著者らは「adaptive black-box cost control」として位置づけており、モデル内部を触らずに環境適応する方向性を示している。固定のプロンプト最適化や出力圧縮とは補完関係にあり、RTKとの組み合わせでさらに削減した報告もある。

【出典と確認方法】
- 論文：https://t.co/dCBZO3tqFh
- コード：https://t.co/eYVsSvDWFw（Apache-2.0、Python 3.10+）
- プロジェクトページ：https://t.co/eeS3LsbLY0
- インストール例（Claude Code）：
  git clone https://t.co/OlQSRjmvf6
  claude plugin marketplace add "$PWD/TokenEconomizer"
  claude plugin install tokeneconomizer@tokeneconomizer

GitHub上のスター数は公開後急速に伸び、11月上旬時点で5,000前後まで到達している。一次情報を直接確認し、自分のリポジトリでstatusコマンドを叩いてみるのが最も確実な検証だ。

#TokenEconomizer #MicrosoftResearch #ClaudeCode #Codex #AIエージェント #トークン削減 #SWE-Bench #OSS

items.title: I try pretty much every new AI model that drops and these are the only ones I'd bother with right now:
items.summary:
I try pretty much every new AI model that drops and these are the only ones I'd bother with right now:

1. GPT-6.1 Sol

> Orchestration and agent planning
> Same price as Sonnet, but more powerful
> Insanely token efficient

2. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash

> Cheap, high-volume AI tasks
> Good enough for most routine work
> Use it when token costs matter

3. Gemini 3.8 Flash

> Reading images and screenshots
> Accurate visual understanding at low cost
> Fast enough for high-volume image processing

4. GPT Image 2.6

> High-quality image generation and editing
> Sunburst for quality, Flare for speed
> Great for creating and editing visuals

5. Exa 3.0 Lite

> Super fast web search for AI agents
> Cheap enough for high-volume searches
> Only pull the context you need

There's a ridiculous number of AI models out there now.

But I genuinely struggle to find a good reason to use most of them.

The best model isn't always the smartest one. It's the cheapest one that reliably gets the job done.

Stop using frontier models for everything.

items.title: Fable 5.2 降价了，为什么还有人觉得更烧钱？
items.summary:
Fable 5.2 降价了，为什么还有人觉得更烧钱？

Mian（@themianoo）用了几个小时，吐槽三件事：能力割裂、审美退步、Token 消耗离谱。这些是个人体感，不是统一测试结论。

我更在意背后的落差：用户买的是“把活干完”，厂商公布的是“每百万 token 多少钱”。这根本不是一笔账。

我查了官方价格和第三方评测，没亲测。几个容易传歪的地方，拆开说。

1）降价20%是真的，“消耗是上一代4倍”没找到依据。

标准API，每百万token，输入/输出：
Fable 5.1：$10/$50
Fable 5.2：$8/$40
Opus 5.5：$4/$20

5.2确实比5.1便宜20%，也确实是Opus的两倍。但缓存读取，5.2和Opus都是$0.20；5分钟缓存写入分别$10和$5，别把写入也按读取价算。

回复里的@ModelPodAI说对了这组单价；但“长会话通常不到两倍”有前提：两边用量结构相近、确实大量命中缓存。它披露自己运营API平台，有利益相关，这里不采用它的促销报价。

第三方Artificial Analysis的Max、Default Fallback配置下：
• 全套评测输出量：5.2为275M，5.1为163M，约1.69倍。
• 加权每任务输出量：274k对118k，约2.32倍。
• 加权每任务成本：$26.54对$12.99，约2.04倍。

总量与加权每任务不是同一口径，不能混着算；这些也不是你修一次bug的报价。但它们确实支持“单价降了，特定配置下任务成本反而涨了”。不支持把“4倍”当成所有任务的定律。

官方另称，Medium档在难任务上比5.1更省token。这是厂商自测。讨论贵不贵，不报effort档位，结论可能正好相反。

2）编程分数是真的，“其他推理掉回GPT-3.5”证据不够。

49.1%、45.5%、42.8%来自Anthropic的FrontierCode 2.0表，依次是Fable 5.2、Opus 5.5、GPT-6 Astra。49.1%是Xhigh档，不是默认体验，更不是所有编程题的胜率。

非编码也不是一片空白：AA的HLE-Diamond，5.2为80.2%，5.1为60.1%。这不能保证它会做你的非标题，但也不能据几个翻车案例，就认定非编码能力整体退回GPT-3.5。我没找到支持这种跨代断言的对照测试。

审美则保留为个人评价：功能做完和“看着舒服”，本来就是两套验收标准。

3）算一笔你能复现的账。

假设一次多轮agent任务，所有请求累计、分类不重叠：普通输入10万、5分钟缓存写入10万、缓存读取100万、输出2万token。纯假设，不是实测；按标准API，不含工具费、税等。

Fable：0.1×8＋0.1×10＋1×0.20＋0.02×40＝$2.80
Opus：0.1×4＋0.1×5＋1×0.20＋0.02×20＝$1.50

同样用量，差1.87倍，不是整两倍。可如果Fable输出变成8万，其他不变，就是$5.20。缓存能省旧上下文的钱，救不了无限增长的输出和重试。

反过来，贵模型一次过，便宜模型返工三次，也可能前者更省。真正该比的是“全部尝试花费÷验收通过数”，再加上你收拾残局的时间。

原帖还有“Pro额度20多倍、成本仅DeepSeek的1/10”，我没找到可复现的计算。订阅额度和API账单不是同一计价体系，不混算。

自己测并不复杂：同一个任务、同一份初始文件和验收标准，两个模型各跑一遍，固定effort、工具和缓存策略；把全过程usage加总，失败重试也算，别只截最后一次回复。

Claude API重点看input_tokens、output_tokens、cache_creation_input_tokens、cache_read_input_tokens。缓存写入区分5分钟/1小时；这些输入类别分开计费，别重复相加收费。控制台也能核账。一次只能算样本，多跑几次才知道稳不稳。

我的判断：这类吐槽值得听，但别让“4倍”和“降价20%”替你做决定。你不缺一张排行榜，缺的是自己的任务账单。

有实测的可以按“任务／模型+effort／普通输入、缓存写入、读取、输出／总费用／是否验收通过”留一组。这样的评论，比一句“变笨了”更能帮别人选。

items.title: on SimpleQA o4-mini scores 24% and gpt-5-thinking-mini scores 22%. the accuracy leaderboard says o4-mini wins. it's also
items.summary:
on SimpleQA o4-mini scores 24% and gpt-5-thinking-mini scores 22%. the accuracy leaderboard says o4-mini wins. it's also wrong on 75% of questions vs 26% for the newer one

that gap is most of why models make stuff up instead of saying idk

1. almost every benchmark grades right or wrong. a blank and a wrong answer both score 0, so guessing a birthday gets a 1 in 365 shot and "i don't know" gets nothing
2. the OpenAI hallucination paper checked 10 big benchmarks (GPQA, MMLU-Pro, SWE-bench, HLE...). 9 give zero credit for abstaining
3. take two models that know the same facts. one says idk when unsure, the other always guesses. the guesser scores higher on every one of those benchmarks
4. post-training chases those scores, so every model gets pushed toward the guesser
5. gpt-5-thinking-mini abstains on 52% of SimpleQA. that's where its 26% error rate comes from, and plain accuracy can't see it

the fix they propose is kinda old school. put a confidence target in the prompt. at 75%, a wrong answer costs 2 points, so guessing only pays when the model is actually 75% sure. the JEE and the old SAT already graded like this

i think this matters more than any RAG patch, since it changes what labs optimize for

items.title: Meta’s AI age-check goes global: Can it protect teens? | Mental Health News | Al Jazeera
items.summary:
Meta has rolled out artificial intelligence (AI)-powered age-estimation technology worldwide in an effort to better detect teenage users who signed up for its social media platforms with an adult’s birth date.

The world’s largest social media company announced the change on Monday, saying that millions more young people worldwide would be placed in its Teen Accounts following the implementation of the new technology amid concerns that its platforms have failed to protect teenagers. [...] The AI searches a user’s account to find “contextual clues” that point to their age. Examples given by Meta include “birthday celebrations or mentions of school grades”.

It also uses “visual cues” in pictures and videos on the account, but Meta says that this does not extend to facial recognition. [...] Meta, which owns Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and Threads, said on Monday that it had started using its AI age-estimation system on Instagram accounts around the world.

“Since first introducing this technology, we’ve been placing more teens in age-appropriate protections and are encouraged by the results. Based on that success, today we’re expanding this technology globally,” the company said.

items.title: He’s using AI to screen existing compounds for therapeutic potential | University of Pittsburgh
items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của hàm số \( x^2 \) được tính bằng cách sử dụng quy tắc tích phân cơ bản. Nguyên hàm của \( x^n \) (với \( n \neq -1 \)) là:

\[
\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C
\]

Trong trường hợp này, với \( n = 2 \):

\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Vậy nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là:

\[
\frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Trong đó \( C \) là hằng số tích phân.

items.title: Meta’s AI age-check goes global: Can it protect teens? | Mental Health News | Al Jazeera
items.summary:
Meta has rolled out artificial intelligence (AI)-powered age-estimation technology worldwide in an effort to better detect teenage users who signed up for its social media platforms with an adult’s birth date.

The world’s largest social media company announced the change on Monday, saying that millions more young people worldwide would be placed in its Teen Accounts following the implementation of the new technology amid concerns that its platforms have failed to protect teenagers. [...] The AI searches a user’s account to find “contextual clues” that point to their age. Examples given by Meta include “birthday celebrations or mentions of school grades”.

It also uses “visual cues” in pictures and videos on the account, but Meta says that this does not extend to facial recognition. [...] Meta, which owns Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and Threads, said on Monday that it had started using its AI age-estimation system on Instagram accounts around the world.

“Since first introducing this technology, we’ve been placing more teens in age-appropriate protections and are encouraged by the results. Based on that success, today we’re expanding this technology globally,” the company said.

items.title: He’s using AI to screen existing compounds for therapeutic potential | University of Pittsburgh
items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary: Today, we are introducing Gemini Robotics 2.5, our most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date. Gemini Robotics 2.5 increases both the breadth of skills a robot can learn and the speed at which it can acquire them. This enhances dexterity, reliability, and safety to help robots step out of the lab and into more unstructured, real-world environments, where they can assist people with a greater range of tasks. [...] Using our embodied reasoning model (Gemini Robotics ER) to keep track of the workflow, and the Gemini Robotics 2.5 actions model to control its hands and arms, the robot reaches into supply bins, picks up metal automotive brackets, and places them into sequencing containers, all while correcting for any gaps. Achieving a 96% success rate, this pilot shows promising progress toward widespread real-world industrial applications. [...] Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses inference-time reasoning guidance to steer around physical hazards in real-time. Much like safety classifiers add a protective layer around Gemini’s responses, this guidance allows the robot to navigate complex environments securely. In our evaluations, this capability boosted safe task completion around obstacles by 33% and around nearby people by 43%.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

[...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
Even before OpenAI launched ChatGPT in late 2022, some company staffers raised concerns internally about its security practices, according to five people familiar with the matter. Employees shared their concerns with top OpenAI leaders ​and the board of directors, the people said, adding that some staffers came away from those interactions concluding that management was more focused on keeping pace with competitors like Google and Anthropic than on security. [...] Another issue is that OpenAI had not done regular security reviews of its internal tools, such as the so-called sandboxes where researchers stress-test new models, three people familiar with the company’s practices said. Employees often modified those tools for their work, but those changes were not always tested for security problems, leaving them potentially vulnerable to attacks from outsiders, the three people said. [...] OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people.
